settings.heading: The Science of Internal Skin Health
settings.body:
Skin is not an isolated surface. It is a living organ influenced by nutrition, environmental exposure, immune signaling, oxidative stress, the intestinal microbiome, and the integrity of its own barrier.

Alchemia MD formulates around those interconnected systems.

Every ingredient is selected for a defined purpose and evaluated against published research. The goal is not to replace topical skincare or sun protection. It is to add evidence-informed nutritional support to a complete skin-health routine.

settings.heading: Research first. Claims second.
settings.body: Not all scientific evidence is equal. Alchemia MD evaluates ingredients using the totality of available research, with greater weight given to controlled human studies and systematic reviews than to laboratory or animal findings.
settings.note: Ingredient research is not the same as finished-product clinical testing. Research presented on this page describes published studies on individual ingredients or biological pathways. Unless specifically stated otherwise, these studies were not conducted on Alchemia MD finished products.

settings.title: Human clinical research
settings.text: Randomized controlled trials and other controlled human studies provide the most directly relevant evidence for how an ingredient may behave in people.

settings.title: Systematic reviews
settings.text: Reviews and meta-analyses help determine whether findings remain consistent across multiple studies.

settings.title: Mechanistic research
settings.text: Cellular and biochemical studies help explain how an ingredient may influence pathways involved in skin barrier function, oxidative stress, microbiome signaling, or other biological processes.

settings.title: Emerging evidence
settings.text: Promising early research is described as exactly that: promising, but not definitive.

settings.title: Environmental stress
settings.text:
UV and other environmental exposures can influence oxidative stress and cellular responses in skin.

Research on ingredients such as nicotinamide and Polypodium leucotomos has examined biological responses to UV exposure in human volunteers.

settings.title: Skin barrier
settings.text:
The outer skin barrier depends heavily on lipids including ceramides, free fatty acids, and cholesterol.

Experimental research has shown that nicotinamide can increase synthesis of several of these lipids in keratinocytes.

settings.title: Gut–skin axis
settings.text:
The intestine and skin communicate through microbial metabolites, immune signaling, barrier integrity, and other systemic pathways.

The gut-skin axis is an active area of research, although the clinical effects of probiotics remain strain- and formulation-specific.

settings.title: Antioxidant and nutritional support
settings.text:
Different antioxidants and micronutrients act through different biological mechanisms.

Rather than relying on one compound, Alchemia MD formulas combine ingredients selected to provide complementary nutritional and biochemical roles.

settings.heading: UV Shield+
settings.subhead: Nutritional support for skin exposed to life outdoors.
settings.intro:
UV Shield+ combines five ingredients selected around different aspects of environmental and oxidative-stress biology.

The formulation rationale is coverage of several different biological pathways, rather than one single proven ingredient pair.
settings.ingredients:
Niacinamide
Polypodium leucotomos
Trans-resveratrol
Green tea polyphenols / EGCG
Spirulina
settings.note: Research presented here describes studies on individual ingredients, not on UV Shield+ as a finished product. UV Shield+ is not a sunscreen and does not replace sun protection.

settings.name: Niacinamide
settings.subtitle: Vitamin B3
settings.why: Nicotinamide takes part in cellular energy metabolism and has been studied in relation to UV-response biology and skin barrier function.
settings.shows:
A randomized, double-blind crossover study in healthy volunteers found that oral nicotinamide reduced UV-induced suppression of a measured skin immune response at the doses studied.

Separate laboratory and topical research found that nicotinamide increased synthesis of ceramides, free fatty acids, and cholesterol involved in epidermal barrier function.
settings.context: The barrier-lipid study included cell-culture and topical application research. It is not proof that oral UV Shield+ produces the same effect.

settings.name: Polypodium leucotomos
settings.subtitle: Fern-derived botanical extract
settings.why: Polypodium leucotomos has been studied as an oral botanical in relation to skin responses to ultraviolet exposure.
settings.shows:
In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of healthy adults, oral Polypodium leucotomos was evaluated for UV-response endpoints over the study period.

Earlier human research also evaluated oral Polypodium leucotomos in experimentally UV-exposed skin, and newer controlled studies have continued to investigate it in healthy volunteers.

settings.name: Trans-resveratrol
settings.subtitle: Polyphenol
settings.why: Resveratrol is a polyphenol studied for antioxidant, cellular-signaling, and skin-related effects.
settings.shows: A randomized, placebo-controlled study in women aged 40 and older evaluated oral and topical trans-resveratrol over eight weeks and measured several skin parameters, including moisture, elasticity and sebum.
settings.context: The dose and study design differ from UV Shield+. It supports ingredient rationale rather than establishing finished-product efficacy.

settings.name: Green tea polyphenols / EGCG
settings.subtitle: Catechins
settings.why: Green tea catechins have antioxidant properties and have been studied in connection with skin exposed to environmental stress.
settings.shows: Human research on oral green tea polyphenols has produced mixed results. A two-year randomized placebo-controlled study found some interim changes in selected clinical parameters but did not find oral green tea polyphenols superior to placebo for overall clinical or histologic photoaging outcomes after 24 months.
settings.language: We include mixed and null findings on purpose.

settings.name: Spirulina
settings.subtitle: Blue-green algae
settings.why: Spirulina contains proteins, minerals, carotenoids, and phycocyanin, and contributes a different nutritional and antioxidant profile from the formula's polyphenols.
settings.language: Included for its nutritional and antioxidant profile while human skin-specific research continues to develop.

settings.heading: Skinbiotic+
settings.subhead: Synbiotic support built around the gut–skin connection.
settings.intro:
Skinbiotic+ pairs a fermentable prebiotic with multiple microbial strains.

The formulation rationale is the prebiotic and probiotic pairing, and the complementary ecological roles of different organisms.
settings.ingredients:
Organic inulin
Lactobacillus plantarum
Bifidobacterium lactis
Lactobacillus rhamnosus
Bifidobacterium bifidum
Akkermansia muciniphila
settings.feature_body:
The gut-skin axis describes communication between the intestinal environment and the skin through pathways that can include microbial metabolites, immune signaling, barrier integrity, and systemic metabolism.

The concept has substantial biological support, but probiotic outcomes cannot be generalized across every strain or every product. Reviews consistently emphasize variability between organisms, populations, doses, and clinical endpoints.
settings.note: Research presented here describes studies on individual strains and ingredients, not on Skinbiotic+ as a finished product.

settings.name: Inulin
settings.subtitle: Prebiotic fiber
settings.why: Inulin is a fermentable carbohydrate that can serve as food for certain intestinal microorganisms. Its role in Skinbiotic+ is foundational: it forms the prebiotic side of a synbiotic formulation.

settings.name: Lactobacillus plantarum
settings.subtitle: Probiotic strain
settings.why: Different strains of the same species can behave differently.
settings.shows: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 110 adults evaluated Lactobacillus plantarum HY7714 for 12 weeks and reported changes in several measured skin parameters.
settings.context: This evidence is specific to the HY7714 strain. It does not prove identical outcomes for every L. plantarum strain.

settings.name: Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium species
settings.subtitle: Probiotic strains
settings.why: Different microorganisms occupy different ecological niches and produce different metabolites. The formula rationale is broader microbiome support rather than assuming every species provides the same function.
settings.shows: Clinical reviews of probiotic interventions in dermatology point to potential effects through gut-skin signaling, but repeatedly note substantial heterogeneity across strains, formulations, study populations, and outcomes.

settings.name: Akkermansia muciniphila
settings.subtitle: Next-generation probiotic
settings.why: Akkermansia is an emerging microbiome organism studied extensively in intestinal barrier and metabolic biology. Its skin-specific evidence is primarily emerging and preclinical.
settings.language: Included as a next-generation microbiome component while human skin-specific research continues to develop.

settings.heading: Dermaboost+
settings.subhead: Multi-nutrient support for antioxidant, immune, and skin-resilience pathways.
settings.intro:
Dermaboost+ brings together eight ingredients with complementary roles.

The formulation rationale describes several plausible complementary relationships, such as quercetin with curcumin, quercetin with vitamin C, and vitamin C with zinc. These are complementary mechanisms, not proven clinical synergy of the finished formula.
settings.ingredients:
Niacinamide
Vitamin D3
Vitamin C
Zinc
Quercetin
Optimized curcumin
Olive leaf extract
Astaxanthin
settings.note: Research presented here describes studies on individual ingredients, not on Dermaboost+ as a finished product.

settings.name: Astaxanthin
settings.subtitle: Carotenoid
settings.why: Astaxanthin is a carotenoid studied for antioxidant activity and skin-related endpoints.
settings.shows:
A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized human studies found significant pooled effects for moisture and elasticity, while the effect on wrinkle depth was not statistically significant compared with placebo.

A separate randomized controlled study evaluated oral astaxanthin during a 16-week period of seasonal environmental stress.

settings.name: Curcumin
settings.subtitle: Optimized extract
settings.why: Curcumin has been widely investigated for its effects on cellular signaling and oxidative-stress pathways. The formulation uses an optimized form because conventional curcumin has limited oral bioavailability.
settings.shows: Published pharmacokinetic reviews have compared enhanced-bioavailability curcumin preparations with conventional curcumin. Claims about bioavailability should remain formulation-specific and measured rather than assumed.

settings.name: Vitamin C
settings.subtitle: Essential nutrient
settings.why: Vitamin C is an essential nutrient with established physiological roles. It participates in collagen biosynthesis and antioxidant systems.

settings.name: Quercetin
settings.subtitle: Plant flavonoid
settings.why: Quercetin is a plant flavonoid studied for antioxidant and cellular-signaling properties.
settings.shows: Human pharmacokinetic studies confirm oral absorption of quercetin-containing preparations, while much of the skin-specific mechanistic rationale remains derived from laboratory research.

settings.name: Zinc
settings.subtitle: Essential mineral
settings.why: Zinc is an essential mineral that acts as a cofactor for numerous enzymes and contributes to normal immune and cellular functions.

settings.name: Vitamin D3
settings.subtitle: Cholecalciferol, from lichen
settings.why: Vitamin D is an essential nutrient that contributes to normal immune function. The form used here is plant-derived, from lichen.

settings.heading: Different pathways. One skin-health system.
settings.body: The strongest formulation argument is not that one ingredient does everything. It is the opposite: different ingredients and products address different parts of a larger biological system.
settings.caption: This systems model represents formulation rationale. It does not mean the combination itself has been studied in human trials as an Alchemia MD finished-product regimen.

settings.title: UV Shield+ + Skinbiotic+
settings.subtitle: Environmental + microbiome
settings.text: The two formulas operate through different upstream mechanisms: one emphasizes environmental and oxidative-stress pathways, the other targets the intestinal microbial environment. Complementary support from two different biological directions.

settings.title: UV Shield+ + Dermaboost+
settings.subtitle: Environmental + systemic nutritional support
settings.text: These formulas share antioxidant-related ingredients but use different ingredient combinations and pathway emphasis. This is the most prominent two-product overlap in oxidative-stress and immune-response biology.

settings.title: Skinbiotic+ + Dermaboost+
settings.subtitle: Microbiome + nutritional support
settings.text: Skinbiotic+ is oriented toward the gut and microbial interface, while Dermaboost+ contains nutrients and plant compounds selected around broader antioxidant and immune-support pathways.

settings.title: All three: Protect. Balance. Restore.
settings.subtitle: The complete system
settings.text: The complete system spans environmental stress, the intestinal microbiome, and systemic oxidative and immune pathways, with overlap between formulas rather than identical roles.

settings.legend: Dots show the maturity of the evidence, not the effect of any Alchemia MD product.

settings.heading: Good science has boundaries.
settings.not_items:
A supplement can stand in for sunscreen.
Taking a supplement makes prolonged sun exposure safe.
Every ingredient study proves the same result at every dose.
Research on one probiotic strain automatically applies to another.
A study of an isolated ingredient proves the finished formula produces the same outcome.
Laboratory findings are equivalent to randomized human trials.
Supplements are intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.
settings.does_text:
There is published science supporting the biological rationale behind the ingredients and pathways used in Alchemia MD formulations.

That is the level at which this page makes the case.

settings.heading: Internal support is one layer.
settings.body: Alchemia MD is designed to complement, not replace, a complete sun-safety routine.
settings.items:
Broad-spectrum sunscreen
Protective clothing
Shade
Hats and sunglasses
Appropriate reapplication
Routine dermatologic care
settings.callout: A supplement is not sun protection.

settings.text: No single ingredient governs skin health.

settings.text: Ingredients are selected to provide different nutritional or biological functions rather than simply increasing the number on the label.

settings.title: Defined formulas
settings.text:
UV Shield+: Protect. Environmental and antioxidant support.

Skinbiotic+: Balance. Microbiome and gut-skin support.

Dermaboost+: Restore. Antioxidant, nutritional, and immune support.

settings.title: Full transparency
settings.text: You should know what is in a formula and why it is there.

settings.heading: Science should make skin health easier to understand, not harder.
settings.body: The purpose of Alchemia MD is not to overwhelm people with studies. It is to take what we know about skin biology, nutrition, and prevention and translate it into a routine people can actually understand and follow.

settings.heading: Build your internal skin health routine.
settings.body: Understand what each formula is designed to support and choose the level of support that fits your routine.
settings.note: Alchemia MD supplements complement, but do not replace, sunscreen, appropriate sun-protective behavior, or professional medical care.
